user.title: Roomstat
user.description: One entry controls exactly one Tado radiator thermostat (TRV). If a room has several radiators, add one entry per TRV and point them all at the same room temperature sensor.

data_description.source_entity_id: The climate entity of the valve head mounted on the radiator. Do not select a wall thermostat here. For Tado V3+, pick the one from the HomeKit Device integration. Each TRV can only be used by one entry.
data_description.external_temperature_entity_id: A temperature sensor placed in the room, away from the radiator. Use the same sensor for every entry belonging to that room.
data_description.name: Name of the proxy thermostat. Pick a descriptive name per radiator, for example "Lounge Window" and "Lounge Wall", so you can find the entities again in automations.

error.temp_not_a_sensor: Please select a sensor entity as the external temperature sensor.
error.temp_not_temperature: Please select a temperature sensor (device_class: temperature).

abort.already_configured: This radiator thermostat (TRV) is already used by another entry. Each TRV can only be controlled by one proxy.

data_description.external_temperature_entity_id: A temperature sensor placed in the room, away from the radiator. Use the same sensor for every entry belonging to that room.
data_description.boost_duration: How long boost mode stays active before returning to the previous preset.
data_description.summer_mode_entity_id: Optional on/off helper (input boolean) shared by all thermostats. While it is on, this thermostat is locked at 5 °C: window, presence and every change from the UI or automations are ignored. When it turns off, the thermostat returns to Comfort.

data_description.window_sensor_id: Binary sensor that detects an open window. When triggered, heating is paused.
data_description.window_delay_s: Delay before heating is paused after the window opens.
data_description.window_close_delay_s: Minimum delay before heating resumes after the window closes. Heating then waits until the room has stopped re-warming on its own (rising below 1 °C/h), at most 30 minutes after the close. 0 resumes at once.

data_description.presence_sensor_id: Binary sensor or input boolean for presence detection (on = home, off = away). Switches to away mode when it turns off.
data_description.presence_away_delay_s: Delay before switching to away mode after presence is lost.
data_description.presence_home_delay_s: Delay before switching back to comfort mode after presence is detected.

data_description.schedule_entity_id: Optional input select set by your scheduler. Its state is the preset this room should follow: comfort, night, away or frost_protection. Leave empty to use presets manually.
data_description.schedule_override_min: How long a manual change (preset, temperature, boost) overrides the schedule. 0 = until the schedule changes. Otherwise the override ends after this time or at the next schedule change, whichever comes first.

pi_controller.name: Controller
pi_controller.description: Heat-ups run at full power and stop early enough for the radiator's leftover heat to reach the target. Near the target, the valve's setpoint is adjusted firmly and the valve is shut a little ahead of an overshoot.

data_description.correction_kp: How firmly the valve is pushed near the target: by (1 + Kp) × the room's error. A Tado reacts late and only partly to small changes, so this is high. Typical 3–6.
data_description.correction_ki: Corrects a lasting offset near the target. Higher values correct it faster.
data_description.integral_deadband_c: The integral only builds up when the room is this close to the target, so heat-ups never wind it up.
data_description.derivative_time_min: How far ahead Roomstat predicts where the radiator's leftover heat will carry the room, and so how early heating stops, in heat-ups and near the target (there at least 10 min). 0 = no anticipation in heat-ups. When auto-tune learns braking, this is only its starting value.

autotune.name: Auto-tune
autotune.description: Learns Kp, Ki and the braking time for this room in the background, from everyday heat-ups. The values above are the starting point; learned values stay within safe limits around them.

data_description.autotune_enabled: Adjusts the controller a little at a time and undoes any change that makes things worse. Changing Kp, Ki or the braking time above restarts learning.
data_description.autotune_derivative: Also learn how early to stop heating before the target, from how long the radiator keeps heating after Tado is told to stop. Recommended.

trv_communication.name: TRV Communication
trv_communication.description: The thermostat, command timing, battery conservation, a fallback for when the TRV is unavailable, and a time limit on full-power commands.

data_description.source_entity_id: The climate entity Roomstat reads and commands: the valve via HomeKit, or the room's Tado cloud thermostat. To stop using HomeKit, pick the cloud thermostat here; if it was the fallback, the fallback is removed. A cloud thermostat is updated by polling, so Roomstat waits longer before it re-sends a command that has not shown up.
data_description.min_command_interval_s: Minimum time between commands sent to the TRV (battery conservation).
data_description.min_change_threshold_c: Minimum difference to the current Tado setpoint before a new command is sent.
data_description.overlay_refresh_s: Periodically resend the setpoint to the TRV to keep cloud-API overlays alive. 0 = off. Not needed with HomeKit: Roomstat checks every minute that the TRV still holds its command and sends it again if not.
data_description.fallback_entity_id: Optional. Another climate entity for the same room, for example the room's Tado cloud thermostat. While the TRV above is unavailable (such as a HomeKit dropout), Roomstat reads and commands the room through this one instead, and switches back on its own. Auto-tune keeps learning from the room sensor meanwhile.
data_description.prefer_fallback: Command the room through the fallback thermostat above (for example the Tado cloud), and through the TRV only while the fallback is unavailable. For when the local link drops out more often than the cloud. Every command then costs Tado API calls, so it needs enough daily quota (Auto-Assist). The TRV's own reading still feeds auto-tune while it is available.
data_description.heat_timer_s: Tado cloud thermostats only. Full-power commands go to Tado as a timer of this length, renewed every half while still needed. If Home Assistant, the network or the Tado cloud stop, the zone falls back to its Tado app schedule within this time. Set every Roomstat zone's schedule in the Tado app to 5 °C or Off first, then 3600 s is a good value. 0 = off: full power lasts until the next command. Shorter than 900 s counts as 900 s.

out_of_band.name: Out-of-band alarm
out_of_band.description: The room's Out of band sensor turns on when the room stays too hot or too cold while heating is on (not in summer mode, with no window open and a working room sensor). Use it in a notification.

data_description.band_c: How far from the target counts as out of band.
data_description.band_min: How long the room must stay this much too warm. A room still cooling down after the target was lowered (for example the Night setting) never counts; one that warms up again by this much does, if the radiator did it. A room warmed by the sun with the radiator cold is reported as warm, not as an alarm.
data_description.cold_band_min: How long the room must stay this much too cold. Counted again from every rise of the target, so it should be longer than a normal heat-up.

behaviour.name: Behaviour
behaviour.description: Sensor resilience and urgent cool-down threshold.

data_description.sensor_grace_s: How long to use the last valid reading when the external sensor becomes unavailable.
data_description.urgent_decrease_threshold_c: Bypass rate limiting when the new target is this much below the current Tado setpoint.

error.temp_not_temperature: Please select a temperature sensor (device_class: temperature).

abort.trv_in_use: That thermostat is already used by another Roomstat room.

summer_mode_locked.message: Summer mode is on – this thermostat is locked at 5 °C.

replace.title: Replace {entity_id}
replace.description:
The Roomstat room **{room}** uses `{entity_id}`, but Home Assistant no longer has it. It was probably deleted or renamed.

Pick the entity to use instead. An optional setting can be left empty to stop using it. The room then reloads with the new setting.

abort.entry_removed: This Roomstat room no longer exists.

replace.title: Replace {entity_id}
replace.description:
The Roomstat room **{room}** uses `{entity_id}`, but it is disabled, so it never reports.

Enable it again under Settings → Devices & services → Entities, or pick the entity to use instead. An optional setting can be left empty to stop using it. The room then reloads with the new setting.

abort.entry_removed: This Roomstat room no longer exists.

entity_unavailable.title: {room}: no reading from {entity_id}
entity_unavailable.description:
The Roomstat room **{room}** has had no usable reading from its room sensor `{entity_id}` for {minutes} minutes. The room isn't regulated meanwhile: the radiator keeps its last setting.

Check the sensor (power, battery, network). This repair disappears by itself once the sensor reports again.
